## 席位核对

**REWORK** at head `0a480510`. The L1 follows `references/l1-review-checklist.md` from origin/main.

- The read-only list schema, the per-drill remount (item 8), the `openRecord` history-state shape and the shared `emitBucketDrill` read correctly.

The card's own headline acceptance case is not met, and it was never run.

### 1. A relationship-path dimension shows as an unexplained 「View filter」 chip, with no column. This is the card's first acceptance case.

- The card's acceptance opens with HotCRM 「高管总览」 → 「行业收入分布」 donut. It expects a chip such as 「行业 是 科技」 and the default columns 商机名称、行业、金额.
- That widget's dimension is `account_industry`. HotCRM `src/sales/datasets/opportunity.dataset.ts` declares it as `field: 'crm_account.industry'`, a relationship path.
- On this head that slice resolves through `resolveDatasetDrillFilter` to a nested `{ crm_account: { industry: … } }`.
  - `drillListConditions` (`rowsOf`) cannot make a row of it, so it goes to the list's base `filter`.
  - `readViewConditions` (`plugin-list/src/conditions/conditionModel.ts`) reads an object-form filter as one keyless chip. `viewChipText` draws that chip as the generic `listConditions.chips.viewFilter`, which reads 「View filter」.
  - `DatasetWidget` drops dotted fields from `columns`. The defaults are therefore name and amount only.
- So the reader sees a locked 「View filter」 chip that does not say which condition it is, and no industry column. Item 3 (「条件显示出来」) and item 4 both fail on exactly the example the card names.
- The PR body lists this under "Known edges, **not filed**" and calls it "a locked base-filter chip". That is a shipped gap against the acceptance, noticed but not fixed and not carded, under `Fixes #36256`.

**Asked:**
- The dialog must say the condition: at least a locked chip reading the dimension's label and value (「Account Industry: Technology」). Make it an editable chip if the list's rows can carry the path.
- Show the related value as a default column if the list can draw a path column. Otherwise use the lookup field (`crm_account`), and say which in the body.
- Pin the `crm_account.industry` case.
- If part of this really cannot be done in the list, file a card for that part and name it in the body. The seat then decides between `Fixes` and `Part of`.

### 2. Live acceptance owed, on HotCRM

The walk ran on `examples/app-crm`. The card's acceptance names HotCRM. Three of its items were not walked:
- the report page 「各阶段商机」, bar against its summary-table number (body: "not walked in the browser");
- the global filter set to 「上季度」, then a chart drilled, with the chip carrying the date condition and the record count equal to the chart's number (not mentioned);
- the industry donut from item 1.

Please make one live run on HotCRM, on the fixed head, covering:
- the industry donut slice, a 「收入趋势」 month and the 「年度累计收入」 tile;
- the report bar and the summary number opening the same records;
- the global-filter count match;
- a record name opening its page with 「第 1 条，共 N 条」.

Put the dialog shot and the record-page stepper shot in the PR body, as the acceptance asks. The project-files folder alone does not satisfy that line.

### Not asked in this round

- #36462 carries the raw `is_not_null` chip label.
- #36500 (main's `masterDetailDetailsMembers` flake) is out of scope.
- A `$or` or unknown operator landing as 「View filter」 is an edge, not this card's example. One sentence in the body is enough.

Re-request L1 on the new head. The review will be a delta on items 1 and 2.

### ① Derived judgments

The published surface this diff adds is exactly the four members the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line names, and each one is right.
- `DrillNavigationValue.openRecord?` (`@object-ui/react`): optional, and its absence keeps the old shape. The context default stays `{}`. Right.
- `DrillRecordOrigin` (`@object-ui/react`): a new exported interface, reached through `context/index.ts`, which re-exports `DrillNavigationContext`. Right.
- `DrillDownDrawerProps.defaultColumns?` (`@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`): optional. The props type reaches the `.d.ts` through the exported `DrillDownDrawer`. Right.
- `DatasetDrillArgs.fields?` (`@object-ui/plugin-report`): optional, on a type the entry point exports. Right. It is emitted only when non-empty, and `summarySubtotals-27975` now pins it.

Nothing else in the diff is published. `RecordListDrillNavigation` gains a required `openRecord`, and `useRecordListDrillNavigation` gains an optional `originLabel`, but neither is exported from `app-shell/src/index.ts`. `DrillRecordList`, `drillListAvailable`, `DRILL_LIST_COMPONENT`, `drillListConditions`, `measuredFieldsOf` and `emitBucketDrill` are not exported from their package entries. The widened `onChartClick` on `useRegistryComponent` is file-local. No accept-set changes: no spec file, no schema and no authorable key is touched, so `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. Dashboard widgets are dataset-only in the spec (`DashboardWidget.dataset` is required since the single-form cutover), so every authored dashboard drill reaches `DatasetWidget`, which this diff moves to the dialog.

The drilled filter is exact. `drillListConditions` only ever splits the composed filter into ANDed parts. A part becomes chip rows only when every operator in it maps to a row operator and every value is a scalar, or a scalar array for `in` and `not_in`. Everything else (`$or`, a relationship path, `null`, an unknown operator) stays whole in `rest`, which becomes the list's base `filter`. The de-duplication drops only a repeated identical (field, operator, value) triple, which ANDs to itself. ListView merges the base filter, the chip group and its other sources under one `and` (`mergeFilterNodes` through `toFilterNode` and `convertFiltersToAST`), so the first read is the drill filter and nothing more. The date rewording is exact too: ListView lowers `before` to the less-than operator and `after` to the greater-than operator, with the value unchanged. Placeholders are resolved once per mount, and the dialog is keyed on `[objectName, filter]`, so a new drill remounts. As the card asks (item 3), a reader can remove a chip and widen the list. Rows stay bounded by the server's read filter, because the list reads through `dataSource.find`.

Hidden fields are not shown. The default columns and Add column both pass through ListView's own `canReadField` and `isDeclaredHidden` screens, the same screens the object list page uses. The drill hands the list field names only. The list is read-only: inline edit, add record, row colour and grouping are off, the view switcher is hidden, and no save-view, add, bulk, edit, delete, sort-change or filter-change callback is passed. The app-shell test runs the real `@object-ui/plugin-list` and pins zero create, update, delete and bulk calls, no non-GET fetch and no `localStorage.setItem`.

Opening a record and coming back: `openRecord` navigates to `/apps/{app}/{object}/record/{id}`. Its history state carries `from = {pathname + search, label, siblings, total}`, the shape a list already hands the record page. `total` is written only when it is at least the sibling count. The test `useOpenRecordList.drillRecordPage-36256` pins 2 of 3, then 3 of 3, then back to the dashboard URL with its query. `RecordDetailView` is unchanged. The dialog closes after the navigation, so no panel is stacked.

S1 (should-fix): `DrillDownDrawer` is published and also mounted outside the dashboard and report views, by the `object-metric` and `object-pivot` page blocks with an authored `drillDown`. Only `DashboardView` and `ReportView` provide a `DrillNavigationProvider`, so on a page `openRecord` is absent. The new list body then gets `rowOpensRecord={false}` and no `onRowClick`. ListView routes nothing by itself for a host with no row handler, so a drilled row on a page now opens nothing. Before this diff, the drawer's `ObjectDataTable` body opened that row as a record dialog (the removed `drillDown: { enabled: true, mode: 'record', target: 'dialog' }`). The changeset words this removal only for a renderer without `@object-ui/plugin-list`, and the `openRecord` jsdoc says "Absent ⇒ the drill list opens no record". Neither tells a page author that the drill rows lost their record. Fix it either by giving the drill list a way to open a record when the host provides no `openRecord` (for example, the list's own record navigation), or by saying so in the changeset and filing a carrier for the page hosts.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/36256-drill-dialog-standard-list.md` takes `patch` on `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`, `@object-ui/plugin-report`, `@object-ui/react` and `@object-ui/app-shell`. These are the four released packages whose source the diff moves. It carries both line-initial declarations, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the PR body carries the same two lines. Under AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3), a `none` kind takes `patch`, and a widening that is not a protocol change ships `patch`. So the level is right. Check Changeset is green on this head. No major is declared, and nothing is removed or renamed in the type surface, so no migration and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is correct and complete. The claim's original `Clause-②: no` was amended in 7079272440 on the built `.d.ts` reading. The PR body, the changeset and the amendment now agree on the four members judged in ①. The behaviour change in S1 is not a type narrowing: no prop, type or accepted value was taken away. But it belongs in the changeset prose, which is how an upgrading reader learns of it.

### ③ Boundary flags

The area's amendment 7079272440 widened the surface to it, `DashboardView.tsx` and `useOpenRecordList.ts`, and named the TIER_DEFAULT review this record is. The chips and the base filter are ANDed into the one `$filter` that ListView sends to `dataSource.find`, and nothing is fetched and then filtered in the app. The sort, the chip edits and the column calculations are the list's own server reads. The new `siblings` are the ids of rows the list already shows. They travel only as history state for the record page's stepper and never become an `$in` query. No new id materialisation or in-app join is added. The relationship-path drill still resolves through the existing `resolveDatasetDrillFilter` and `resolveRelationshipDrill`, which read no related ids.

Tests against the card's done-when: the dialog's size and lack of overlay, the read-only list, the chips, the default columns, the dialog-local added columns and calculations, the zero writes, the record name to page with 「N of M」 and the way back, the absence of a stacked panel, and the report bar and its summary line opening the same drill are all pinned.

S2 (should-fix): the dashboard half of the card's first acceptance line has no test at the widget. No test drives `DatasetWidget` from a chart mark or a metric tile to the dialog. The new `target="dialog"`, and the default columns it composes (grouped dimension fields without relationship paths, then range fields, then `measuredFieldsOf(scope)`, and `measuredFieldsOf(readMeasureDrillScope(...))` for a tile), are unpinned. `DrillDownDialog-36256` hands `defaultColumns` in by hand. Dropping `target="dialog"` from `DatasetWidget`, or emptying `columns`, would leave every suite green. The report side is pinned (`chartMarkDrill-36256` asserts `fields`); the dashboard side should be pinned the same way, with one chart-mark click and one tile click through `DatasetWidget`, each asserting the dialog and its columns.

N1 (nit): `measuredFieldsOf` exists twice, in `plugin-dashboard/src/drillConditions.ts` and in `plugin-report/src/DatasetReportRenderer.tsx`, with different predicates. The dashboard copy requires `{$null: false}` to be the only key, and the report copy does not. So a bar and a dashboard tile over the same scope could differ in default columns. One shared helper (for example in `@object-ui/core`) would keep them in step.

N2 (nit): the phone branch (`useIsMobile` keeps the drawer) is not pinned. The test "keeps the side drawer and the same list when target is drawer" passes `target: 'drawer'` and never sets a phone viewport, while the PR body lists "Phone keeps the drawer" among the pinned cases.

This is a delta review on the earlier record at `0a480510dd5e5f7da36cb1ad0534cd3ba8cf40b4` (comment 7081517346). Read: card #36256 (body and all seven comments, the round-4 dev report 7082480409 included), PR #36461 (body, the L1 rework note 7081449669, the final-head comment 7082774818), the two first-parent commits since the earlier head (`38e07891811`, `5af2f6e3af2`) and the net diff of 19 files against `main`. Check-runs on this head: 58 in all, 45 success, 13 skipped (the opt-in, schedule and queue-verdict jobs and the Core lanes a ui-only diff does not reach), 0 failed, 0 pending. All 16 Test UI shards, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset, the PR-body guards and the Governed Surface Queue Guard are green.

Earlier findings, by id:

S1: closed. A host with no `openRecord` now opens the drilled record in a dialog from both drill bodies. `DrillRecordList` always passes `rowOpensRecord` and an `onRowClick`, and mounts `RecordDetailDrawer` with `target="dialog"` when the host gives no `openRecord`. The data-table body gets back `drillDown: { enabled: true, mode: 'record', target: 'dialog' }` under the same condition, which is exactly what `main` does. `ObjectMetricWidget.drillOpensRecord-36256` pins both bodies, and `DrillDownDrawer.chain` is split by host kind. What the standard-list arm shows in that dialog is a new finding, S3 below.
S2: closed. `DatasetWidget.drillDialog-36256` drives `DatasetWidget` itself from a chart mark, a metric tile and a relationship-path row, and asserts `target === 'dialog'`, `open` and the composed `defaultColumns` each time. Dropping `target="dialog"` or emptying `columns` now turns it red.
N1: open. `measuredFieldsOf` still exists twice with different predicates. The dev declined a shared helper and the PR body now states the difference and calls it a known edge. That is a stated decision, so nothing more is owed in this PR.

N3: closed. The PR body now shows the dialog shot and the record-page stepper shot inline. Where those images are hosted is the seat's matter and is not judged here.

### ① Derived judgments

The published surface is unchanged since the earlier record: the four additive members named by the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line (`DrillNavigationValue.openRecord?`, `DrillRecordOrigin`, `DrillDownDrawerProps.defaultColumns?`, `DatasetDrillArgs.fields?`), each right. The two new commits add no export. `RecordDetailDrawer` and `DrillRecordList` are still not exported from `plugin-dashboard/src/index.tsx`, and no props type changed in this round. No spec file, schema or authorable key is touched, so `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

The relationship-path column is right. In `DatasetWidget.openDrill` and in the report's `emitBucketDrill`, a grouped dimension whose field is a path (`crm_account.industry`) now contributes its first segment (`crm_account`) to the default columns, where it was dropped before. The first segment of a dataset path is the lookup field on the base object, so the column is a real field of the listed object, and a multi-hop path reduces to the same first hop. The column still passes through ListView's own `canReadField` and `isDeclaredHidden` screens and its FLS-gated `$select`, so a reader who may not read the lookup gets no column and no value. The drilled filter is not touched by this change: the nested condition still comes from `resolveDatasetDrillFilter` and `resolveRelationshipDrill`, and `drillConditions.ts` did not move in this round. Both sides are pinned with the nested condition and `['crm_account', 'amount']`.

The drilled filter and the read-only list are as judged before. No record outside the drilled cell is listed on the first read, and the dialog writes nothing.

The record dialog for a host with no record page shows no hidden value. On the standard-list arm the row it is given holds only what the list's FLS-gated `$select` asked for. On the data-table arm it is the same row and the same drawer as on `main`.

S3 (should-fix): on the standard-list arm, the record dialog for a host with no `openRecord` shows populated fields as empty. `DrillRecordList` hands `RecordDetailDrawer` the clicked list row together with the whole object definition, and no `fields` list. With a definition and no `fields`, the drawer lists every non-system field of the object and draws `EmptyValue` for any key the record lacks. But the row comes from the standard list, whose read is projected: ListView builds `$select` from `schema.columns` (id, the listed columns and the expand roots), and the drill always passes columns. So the row holds only the name, the grouped fields and the measured fields, and every other field of the record reads as empty in the dialog, although it has a value. On `main` this dialog was fed by `ObjectDataTable`, whose read carries no `$select`, so every field showed its value. The comment "as it did before" in `DrillRecordList.tsx` and the PR body's "as these hosts did before" therefore do not hold for the content. The new test does not see it, because its list is a stub and its object has one field. This reading is from the code; nothing was run. The reach is the `object-metric` and `object-pivot` page blocks with an authored `drillDown` in a renderer that registers `@object-ui/plugin-list` (the Console does); dashboards and reports are not affected. Fix it by passing the drawer the fields the list actually fetched (`fields` set to the listed columns, which also restores the authored `drillDown.columns` whitelist that `ObjectDataTable` passes), or by reading the full record before showing it. The drawer's `objectTypesPending` guard, which `ObjectDataTable` passes so that values are masked while field types are unknown, is also not passed here.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right. The changeset `.changeset/36256-drill-dialog-standard-list.md` takes `patch` on `@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`, `@object-ui/plugin-report`, `@object-ui/react` and `@object-ui/app-shell`, the four released packages whose source the diff moves. It carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start, and the PR body carries the same two lines. A widening that is no protocol change ships `patch`. Nothing is removed or renamed in the type surface, so no migration is owed. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is correct and complete against the four members in ①; round 4 added none. Check Changeset is green on this head.
